units.translation: 342-44a. "If me thrice as much": through this especially, as if saying that the hindrance of the journey is from the gods, he persuades them to turn back if anything bad happens to the bird. He says this because we receive the words of the unjust as untrustworthy and unfulfilled on account of their impiety. He says therefore: even if you suspect that I am hated by the gods three times as much or even more than I truly am hated, do not dare to cross without an omen.
b. "Anarsios" means "inharmonious", but it also means "hostile"; for enemies do not agree with one another. P
c. "Parex" with barytone accent is used instead of "chōris" (apart from).
345. "And these things, however they may turn out": and these things would happen thus, just as it will be and is fated. L
346. "The meeting of the rocks": the collision. Through this again he hints rather that their exit is not easy nor without danger.

347-49a. "Straightaway of the Bithynians": for after the island of Phineus, on the right-hand parts is Bithynia along the Bosporus. So for one sailing out quickly, the other side of the mouth of the Pontus is Bithynia; for Bithynia, as has been said, is around the Bosporus on the right, and on the left
is Salmydessus of the wild Thracians. Salmydessus was named from the river that flows into it.

b. "You sail along the breakers": keeping to Bithynia, sail to the right, guarding against the breakers on the left side — he would mean those of Salmydessus, since the Thracians dwelling around Salmydessus used to attack and plunder those sailing past.
c. Rhebas is a river of Bithynia.
d. Melaina: a headland so called. Lg (P)

351-52a. "From there not far": sailing from the island of Thynias, you will come not far across to the land of the Mariandyni. The Boeotians occupied the land of the Mariandyni with Gnesiochus the Megarian, as Ephorus (70 FGrH 44b J.) relates. The river Acheron flows past it. Acheron is named from "achea" (griefs).
b. "Antiperaian" means opposite the island; for the Mariandynian land lies opposite the island. P

353-56a. "There into Hades": along the Acheron in Mariandynia there is a certain descending road as if to the river of Hades. Having violent streams, it cuts through it — Mariandynia —, flowing from below, and flowing from a certain ravine it casts its streams into the headland.
b. "And a projecting headland": a headland at Heraclea, which they call Acherusian
